## Warm-path closure and carried work

The **50 ms predicate is unchanged**. Earlier failures stay failures on their original source. Neither the dedicated profile nor the later interleaved baseline explains their cause. The accepted implementation changes the relevant warm path: it reattaches existing regional/hull handles instead of repeating regional construction. Its declared 56-transition trial measures median/p95/max **0.25/1.2/3.0 ms**, against baseline **11.75/20.2/22.7 ms**, on matching path classes. Root agrees that this supports bounded closure without claiming a diagnosed historical spike or universal maximum.

Two regions draw and four total detailed/retained owners are allowed. This covers all current regions; future eviction and multiple ordinary hulls are not proven. Cold entry remains roughly 272–387 ms; idle preparation is synchronous, with reviewer Canopy/Basin samples 300.2/64.6 ms. Immediate start, graphics restoration and first hull appearance can still construct during a frame. No separate first-entry/menu budget is adopted by this acceptance.

Carry into M2-B before wider world construction: define first-entry/menu responsiveness targets, measure retained memory and eviction, and reassess multi-hull lifetime/obstruction. Retire carrier feasibility controls when earned carrier systems replace them. Give useful Basin cargo an early visible Creel/service payoff; preserve the second membrane habitat and both finite-stock fleet strategies. These are next-stage obligations and design guidance, not claims that this batch implemented them.

Human controls/learning, audible mix, screen-reader speech, enjoyment/duration and representative-GPU results remain unavailable. Source-attributed route/diagnostic and camera limitations remain in the report.
